neet_phy_u04_t02_1.working: The friction deceleration is a = μg = 3 m/s². So d = v²/(2a) = 36/6 = 6 m.

neet_phy_u04_t02_3.working: Loss of PE = 2×10×5 = 100 J. Gain in KE = ½×2×64 = 64 J. Work by friction = 64 − 100 = −36 J.

neet_phy_u04_t02_4.working: Fd = KE, so equal KE and equal force give equal distance: A is true. The work-energy theorem holds for all forces, so R is false.

neet_phy_u04_t02_5.working: I: d ∝ v², so doubling speed gives 4× distance, true. II: W = ∫x dx from 0 to 3 = 4.5 J, so ½v² = 4.5 and v = 3 m/s, true.
